comparison: Both address post-entry restriction claims (C1, C15, C19-C22). OpenEval finds these claims well-supported by multiple experimental approaches. However, Peer Reviewer 1 raises critical concerns about interpretation, suggesting the punctate E1 staining pattern indicates endosomal trapping rather than a later post-entry block, marking this as UNCERTAIN versus OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R2 addresses rescue by early VACV genes (C2, C16, C48-C49, C51-C52) and finds evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R1 partially overlaps (C2, C16) but focuses on post-entry restriction interpretation concerns rather than the rescue mechanism claims.

Both address RNAi pathway restriction (C3, C30-C31). OpenEval finds the RNAi knockdown data SUPPORTED with ~10-fold effects. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of 'novel insights into RNA virus restriction' without challenge, also marking as SUPPORTED.

Both address IMD pathway restriction (C4, C32). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED by RNAi knockdown showing ~10-fold increase. Peer reviewers accept these host restriction pathway findings as SUPPORTED contributions to understanding antiviral responses.

Both address ubiquitin-proteasome system restriction (C5, C33-C35, C47). OpenEval finds strong SUPPORTED evidence from RNAi, chemical inhibitors, and viral deubiquitinase with dramatic 1000-fold effects. Peer reviewers accept these findings as SUPPORTED without specific critique.

Both address A51R identification and necessity (C6, C57-C59, C64-C65). OpenEval finds convergent genetic evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge A51R identification as a key finding, treating it as SUPPORTED: 'The authors identify a previously uncharacterized VACV gene product A51R as being responsible for the rescue.'

Both address A51R sufficiency (C68-C69, C72). OpenEval finds transfection experiments showing ~60-fold increase SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept A51R identification without challenging sufficiency evidence, marking as SUPPORTED.

Both address A51R functional conservation across poxviruses (C80-C81). OpenEval finds conservation across homologs with 30% identity SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this by noting the manuscript identifies 'multiple targets for A51R,' marking as SUPPORTED.

Perfect overlap on cell-type specificity claims (C82-C87). OpenEval finds phylogenetic pattern SUPPORTED with appropriate caution about Drosophila negative results. Peer reviewers accept these findings as SUPPORTED, consistent with statement that 'A51R overcomes immunity mechanisms shared between Lepidopterans and mammals but absent in Dipteran insects.'

Both address A51R microtubule colocalization (C9, C88-C93). OpenEval finds confocal microscopy and drug resistance data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting 'A51R colocalizes with, and stabilizes, host microtubules' as SUPPORTED contribution.

Both address microtubule stabilization (C10, C93, C98-C101). OpenEval finds drug resistance experiments SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept MT stabilization as SUPPORTED, treating it as one of the 'important clues' about A51R function.

Both address A51R-ubiquitin association (C11, C105, C118). OpenEval finds mass spec data SUPPORTED despite technical challenges with A51R insolubility. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'A51R...also associates with ubiquitin' as SUPPORTED, though note mechanism remains 'complex.'

Both address viral protein stability mechanism (C12, C110-C117). OpenEval finds pulse-chase and pulse-labeling data SUPPORTED, showing A51R acts post-translationally. Peer Reviewer 2 directly challenges this as UNSUPPORTED, stating 'the evidence here is not convincing' and requesting proper pulse-chase experiments, noting reduced protein could be due to decreased replication rather than stability effects.

Both address translation rates (C13, C110-C112). OpenEval finds pulse-labeling showing similar translation rates SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 2's critique of protein stability claims (R6) implicitly questions the interpretation of these translation experiments as well, marking as UNSUPPORTED.

Perfect overlap on separation-of-function mutant (C102-C104). OpenEval finds R321A mutant data SUPPORTED, showing MT stabilization is insufficient for full rescue. Peer reviewers accept this as SUPPORTED, consistent with acknowledgment that mechanism is 'vague' but there are 'important clues.'

Perfect overlap on VACV replication in vertebrate cells (C7, C119-C122). OpenEval finds growth curve data showing ~100-fold difference SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept this as SUPPORTED, noting manuscript shows 'A51R is also critical for VACV replication in vertebrate cells.'

Perfect overlap on mouse pathogenesis (C8, C123-C132). OpenEval finds in vivo infection studies with mortality, weight loss, and tissue titer data strongly SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept as SUPPORTED, noting 'A51R is also critical...for pathogenesis in mice' and that attenuation 'may be an important feature of the vaccine strain.'
OpenEval finds EEV production data (C133-C135) SUPPORTED, showing paradoxically higher EEV release from ΔA51R. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval finds IFN pre-treatment experiments (C136-C138) SUPPORTED, ruling out increased IFN sensitivity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval marks mechanistic proposals about ubiquitin sequestration/deubiquitination (C14, C178-C179, C191, C216) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct biochemical evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative mechanism claims.
OpenEval finds ActD experiments (C23-C29) SUPPORTED but notes confounding apoptosis effects make mechanistic interpretation uncertain. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds differential VACV strain rescue activity (C53-C56) SUPPORTED, helping narrow search to A51R. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval finds VACV-MVA A51R truncation and non-functionality (C60-C62) SUPPORTED by immunoblot and rescue experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds A51R early gene expression timing (C63-C64) SUPPORTED by time-course immunoblots. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds MT-pelleting data and connection to nocodazole-resistant MT pieces (C192-C194) SUPPORTED, though notes unpublished data limits evaluation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds literature summary on MT role in VSV/SINV replication (C195-C200) SUPPORTED with sound reasoning about timing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval marks endosomal trafficking hypotheses (C201-C208) as UNCERTAIN, noting observations are factual but connections to A51R function are inferential. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though Peer R1 does raise endosomal trapping concerns in different context.
OpenEval marks EEV release and vaccine efficacy connections (C209-C214) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation lacks direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval marks mechanistic proposals about Ub sequestration on MT scaffolds (C215-C218) as UNCERTAIN, requiring biochemical validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds extensive background knowledge claims (C17-C18, C36-C38, C45-C46, C50, C106-C108, C134, C139-C177, C181-C182, C218) SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these context claims.

OpenEval marks forward-looking statements about future applications (C161-C162, C185, C219-C221) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are projections rather than demonstrated outcomes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds interpretive conclusions (C165, C167, C180, C183-C184, C186-C190) mostly SUPPORTED by experimental data and literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific interpretive claims.
